script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers

- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

Title: "Pride of Pinewood"

INT. PINEWOOD HIGH SCHOOL - EARLY MORNING

An empty hallway. The sound of JAMES' (25, dedicated) footsteps echoes down the polished tile floor. He wears a letterman's jacket, a relic of his glory days as a high school football star. Now he is the school's Physical Education teacher.

James looks at a photograph of himself in action on the football field, holding the state championship trophy aloft. He sighs, lost in thought.

INT. PE CLASSROOM - MORNING

Students fill the PE classroom. They are reluctant, some already sweating in anticipation of James' demanding exercises.

JAMES
(standing in front of the class)
Attention, class. Today, we will be practicing... soccer.

Murmurs fill the room. Most of the students are shocked. Soccer, they've heard, is for those who aren't 'tough' enough for football. James, though, has a plan.

EXT. PINEWOOD HIGH SCHOOL - GYM FIELD

The students, reluctantly, take to the field. They form a circle, James at the center. He explains the importance of teamwork, communication, and mutual respect.

Suddenly, the sound of a school bus arriving outside interrupts the lesson. The students look up to see a bus filled with children from the local elementary school.

James smiles, reminding them that they have an opportunity to be role models, to inspire the next generation of Pinewood students.

INT. PINEWOOD HIGH SCHOOL - GYM - NIGHT

James sits in the dimly lit gym, staring at a soccer ball. He reflects on the day's events - the unexpected arrival of the elementary school students and the positive impact it had on the older students.

He hears a knock on the door. It's Coach OLIVER (50, wise), the school's basketball coach.

COACH OLIVER
(entering the gym)
James, I heard about today. Nice work.

James smiles, grateful for the recognition. They discuss the potential for a combined soccer team, bringing together students from both elementary and high school.

EXT. PINEWOOD TOWN SQUARE - DAY

The town is bustling with activity. Flyers promoting the new soccer team, "Pride of Pinewood," are pinned up on lampposts and storefronts.

INT. PINEWOOD HIGH SCHOOL - PE CLASSROOM - DAY

James stands before his class, a newfound energy in his eyes.

JAMES
Class, we've got a chance to build something special here. A team, a community, a source of pride for Pinewood. Who's with me?

The students look at each other, their expressions changing from reluctance to excitement. They step forward, forming a circle.

FADE OUT.

TO BE CONTINUED...
